item.title: Electron versus positron impact ionization of inner shells of heavy atoms: distortion, exchange and relativistic effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.31716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triple differential cross sections are presented for electron and positron impact ionization of the K shells of Cu, Ag, Au and U and the L shells of Ag. Relativistic effects are important throughout. For positrons the recoil maximum is suppressed and the recoil-region spin asymmetry changes sign; for the $2s$ shell the binary peak changes. In symmetric geometry, where theory reproduces the measured absolute electron cross section, the positron peak lies on the other side of zero recoil. Measurements would test relativistic ionization theory in a regime that electron experiments cannot reach.
item.dc:creator: Colm T. Whelan

item.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
item.description: arXiv:2611.31772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Under the specified Lindblad conditions, local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization imply that an n-atom connected contribution to the root optical coherence is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. Consequently, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom connected clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions. Direct finite-cluster calculations confirm the predicted lowest allowed orders, while an illustrative Maxwell-propagation calculation shows that triplet contributions can partially oppose pair-induced polarization rotation. Our results establish a rigorous connection between optical perturbation order and the connected many-body sectors that can contribute to it.
item.dc:creator: Lintian Luo, Weixuan Gu, Yan Li

item.title: Perturbation of CO A1{\Pi} by a3{\Pi} should have been undetectable: detection, mechanism, and surprises
item.description: arXiv:2611.32289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A direct perturbation between the $a^3\Pi$ and $A^1\Pi$ vibrational levels of two electronic states that belong to the same electronic configuration of the carbon monoxide molecule should be unobservably weak because the vibrational overlap integral $\langle a^3\Pi,v' \mid A^1\Pi,v'' \rangle$ for their near-degenerate levels is extremely small. Yet level-shift and transition-intensity signatures of the $a^3\Pi(v = 13) \sim A^1\Pi(v = 2)$ perturbation are unmistakably present in the $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{18}\mathrm{O}$ isotopologue. A detailed study of, among others, the $A^1\Pi$ - $X^1\Sigma^+(2, 0)$, $B^1\Sigma^+$ - $A^1\Pi(0, 2)$, and $C^1\Sigma^+$ - $A^1\Pi(0, 2)$ spectra, obtained by the VUV- and Vis-FT complementary techniques in the energy regions of the six crossing points ($e$- and $f$-symmetry, $|\Omega| = 0, 1, 2$) between the $a^3\Pi(v = 13)$ and $A^1\Pi(v = 2)$ states, reveal that the perturbation pathways are indirect, primarily facilitated by the $e^3\Sigma^-(v = 4)$ state, and that quantum mechanical interferences via its F1e and F3e components occur.
item.dc:creator: Stanis{\l}aw Ryzner, Robert W. Field, Wim Ubachs, Alan N. Heays, Asen Pashov, Patryk Jasik, J\'ozef E. Sienkiewicz, Nelson de Oliveira, Kin F. Lai, Marzena I. Malicka, Aleksandra Stasik, Wojciech Szajna, Izabela Piotrowska, Rafa{\l} Hakalla

item.title: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders
item.description: arXiv:2611.32680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mott insulators typically appear at integer densities, but certain lattice geometries or non-local interactions can stabilise Mott insulators at fractional densities. In this work, we study strongly interacting two-leg ladders using ultracold bosonic atoms around half-filling, and identify the rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through its characteristic rung occupation in site-resolved measurements. We probe its excitation spectrum via lattice modulation spectroscopy, and interpret the observed spectra using numerical simulations that include the driven dynamics, coupling to multiple excited states, and energy offsets. As with other Mott insulators, the RMI phase is characterized through its incompressibility, which we probe via a site-resolved analysis of densities and chemical potentials. Our results provide direct insight into the excitation dynamics of a strongly correlated ladder system, and pave the way for studying transport and further dynamical properties in low-dimensional quantum systems with programmable lattice geometries.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Parsonage, Lennart Koehn, Lorenzo Carfora, Ben Watson, Timon Hilker, Elmar Haller, Peter Kirton, Arthur La Rooij, Stefan Kuhr

item.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
item.description: arXiv:2609.18972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $\pi$ pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single $2\pi$ pulse yields a $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(Z)$ gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a $\text{C}_2(Z)$ fidelity of $0.996$ estimated with $T_2^\ast=1.5$~s and a gate duration of $T \approx 4\text{~ms}$. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of $10^{-4}$ for $\mathbb{N}=2,3$ and $10^{-3}$ for $\mathbb{N}=4$, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as $25\hbar/T$.
item.dc:creator: Yan Lu, Xiao-Feng Shi
